fatal_errors: The proposed elevated-temperature constant-stress experiment does not reconstruct the room-temperature nanoindentation-creep study.
It omits modulation period and interface coherency, the central controlled variable and structural mediator.

It attributes resistance to generic HEA sluggish diffusion, whereas the target mechanism centers on semicoherent-interface dislocation pileup and proposed stress-induced interfacial amorphization followed by diffusion or interface slip.
The baselines are single-layer or non-HEA coatings rather than coherent-interface and grain-boundary-dominated versions of the same multilayer system.
No supporting evidence is cited, and intrinsic sluggish diffusion in HEAs is asserted without validation.
explanation: The response addresses time-dependent deformation in HEA multilayers and proposes a controlled creep comparison with a clear falsification rule, so it has some broad problem alignment and experimental testability. However, it misses nearly every distinguishing feature of the target: the Al-Cr-Fe-Ni FCC/BCC multilayers, 8–80 nm modulation-period series, coherent-to-semicoherent-to-grain-boundary transition, room-temperature 5 mN nanoindentation conditions, and stress-exponent analysis. Its generic claim that interfaces impede dislocations overlaps only weakly with the target mechanism. The predicted improvement of multilayers over monolithic or non-HEA controls does not recover the nonmonotonic optimum at 16 nm or the change from dislocation-mediated creep to diffusion/interface-slip behavior. Because the alternative mechanism has no cited support and relies on the contested blanket assumption of sluggish diffusion in HEAs, it is insufficiently evidenced despite being experimentally falsifiable.
